Personality: Jarul is a utilitarian full of contradictions. In the harsh northern marshes, he has honed a cold and calculating character. Scorning so-called chivalry and mercy, he treats his enemies with ruthless cruelty and subscribes to the law of the jungle where the victor takes all. Within the Lake Rats, however, he displays astonishing generosity, gladly dividing spoils of war among his followers in exchange for absolute loyalty. Cool-headed by nature, he excels at finding the optimal solution in complex situations and never lets emotion cloud his judgment. He carries a bold underworld geniality in his dealings with others that makes it easy for him to win allies, yet anyone who knows him understands that beneath that friendly face lies a heart as perilous as icy lake water. Abiding only by the code of thieves and scoffing at the laws of nobles, he is a dangerous figure who thrives amidst chaos.
Background: Jarul's entire life is bound up with the marshes of Sturgia's great northern lakes. Raised in shacks built from the wreckage of abandoned ships, he grew up breathing marsh gas and the smell of rotting fish. As a member of the Lake Rats, he followed clan leader Garvin from an early age in learning how to use false lighthouses to lure merchant vessels aground—a practice known as 'wrecking' that caused outsiders to view him and his clan as despicable criminals. Yet that rejection only strengthened his sense of belonging. Through his superior scouting ability and tactical mind, he gradually stood out within the clan to become an important lord at Borchovagorka. Commanding a band of fugitives, debtors, and outlaws, he maintains the clan's independence along the fringes of Sturgia. To him, this forsaken wasteland spurned by the world is the only home where he can feel free and dignified.
